# 1. Purpose and status

This note records what we learned about the prior on the MSM and heterosexual transmission multipliers
(`transmission.rate.multipliers.by.sex` in `applications/SHIELD/shield_calib_parameters.R`), and the
structural changes we may consider.

1. **Nothing in this note has been changed in the model.** `calib.10.20.stage1` is running with the prior as it is.
2. `calib.10.20.stage1` is the first fit whose likelihood sees male P&S diagnoses by sex before 2019
   (see section 8). Decide on the changes below after it finishes.
3. Numbers from the data were made with `prior/check_spline_prior_against_data.R` and
   syphilis-manager-v2026.10.09. Numbers from the fits come from `calib.10.15.stage3`.

# 2. The prior as it is now

```{r prior-now}
transmission.rate.multipliers.by.sex = make.joint.mv.spline.prior(
    parameters          = paste0("transmission.rate.multiplier.", c("msm", "heterosexual")),
    logmean.baseline    = c(log(3), log(1)),                    # 2000 medians: msm 3, het 1
    logsd.baseline      = c(log(2)*2, log(2)*2),                # 95% range x/÷ 16, msm and het independent
    logsd.deltas.past   = c("1970" = 0.5*log(TRATE_DELTA^2),    # 1970-1990
                            "1990" = 0.5*log(sqrt(TRATE_DELTA)),# 1990-1995
                            "1995" = 0.5*log(sqrt(TRATE_DELTA))),# 1995-2000
    logsd.deltas.future = c("2010" = 0.5*log(TRATE_DELTA),      # 2000-2010
                            "2022" = 0.5*log(TRATE_DELTA)),     # 2010-2022
    spline.times        = c("1970", "1990", "1995", "2000", "2010", "2022"),
    correlation         = 0.7)
# TRATE_DELTA = 1.5
```

How to read it:

1. Each group (MSM, heterosexual) has a value at 2000 (the baseline) and a change ("delta") for each step
   between spline years. Values between spline years are drawn as straight lines.
2. Each change is on the log scale: 0 = no change, +0.69 = doubled, -0.69 = halved.
3. Each change has mean 0 ("no change expected") and an SD set by `TRATE_DELTA`.
4. Within the same step, the MSM and heterosexual changes are correlated (0.7). Different steps are independent.
   The 2000 baselines are independent (the code resets the baseline block to diagonal).

The assumptions, with their current values:

| | Assumption | Current value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spline points | 1970, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2010, 2022 |
| 2 | Baseline medians (2000) | MSM 3, heterosexual 1 |
| 3 | Baseline spread | SD 1.39 (95% x/÷ 16), MSM and het independent |
| 4 | **A. Expected change in each step** | **0** for both groups |
| 5 | Spread of each change | per-group SD 0.405 (1970-1990), **0.101** (each 5-year step), **0.203** (each 10-year step) |
| 6 | **B. How the SD grows with the step length** | **in proportion to years** (5 years = half of 10, 20 years = double) |
| 7 | **C. MSM-het correlation of change** | **0.7**, the same for every step |
| 8 | Steps independent of each other | yes |

The SD of the change in the MSM:heterosexual ratio is the per-group SD x sqrt(2 x (1 - 0.7)) = per-group SD x 0.775:
0.079 for a 5-year step and 0.157 for a 10-year step.

History: `TRATE_DELTA` was 3 at calib.10.1. We lowered it to 1.5 after a calibration gave very high diagnoses
before 1990, and at the same time added the historical diagnosis penalty for 1970-1989. Since 10.15 that
penalty has effective weight 1 in every stage (4-32x stronger than before), so it now holds pre-1990 trends itself.

# 3. Evidence from the fits (calib.10.15.stage3)

## 3.1 Parameters pressed against the prior

Percentile of the posterior median among 10,000 prior draws (`check_prior_and_ps_el_split.R`, now `prior/check_prior_position.R`); flagged below 2.5% (LOW) or above 97.5% (HIGH).

| Change | Flagged |
|---|---|
| MSM - het, 1995-2000 | HIGH in 4 (Chicago, Houston, NYC, Philadelphia); LOW in Phoenix |
| MSM - het, 2000-2010 | HIGH in 5 (Atlanta, Chicago, LA, Miami, NYC) |
| MSM, 1990-1995 | LOW in 3 (Houston, LA, NYC) |
| MSM, 1995-2000 | HIGH in 3 (Houston, Miami, NYC); LOW in Phoenix |
| Het, 2000-2010 | LOW in 2 (LA, NYC) |
| MSM - het, 2010-2022 | LOW in LA only |
| Care-seeking, symptomatic women | LOW in 6 (Houston, LA, Miami, NYC, Phoenix, Seattle) |

Being pressed against the prior is not a problem on its own. It matters only when it comes with a misfit.

## 3.2 The misfit: P&S male:female ratio, model / data (`check_ps_by_sex_over_time.R`, now part of `fit/check_fit_by_sex_over_time.R`)

| Period | Male:female, model / data (range over 10 cities) | Male P&S, model / data |
|---|---|---|
| 1993-1999 | 1.40 - 2.32 (too high everywhere) | 0.90 - 1.86 |
| 2000-2004 | 0.44 - 1.75 | 0.46 - 1.43 |
| 2005-2009 | 0.40 - 1.04 (too low in 9 of 10) | 0.42 - 0.77 |
| 2010-2014 | 0.44 - 0.78 (too low in all) | 0.47 - 0.82 |
| 2015-2019 | 0.49 - 0.86 (too low in all) | 0.59 - 0.88 |

1. In the data, men pull far ahead of women after 2000. In the model they pull ahead much less.
2. **Caveat:** calib.10.15 never had male P&S by sex before 2019 in its likelihood (the mapping bug, section 8).
   Part of this misfit may disappear in calib.10.20.
3. The model's MSM share of male P&S is too high in 6 cities (model 70-90%, data 50-67%, 2016-2021). With male P&S too low
   at the same time, this points to **heterosexual men** being too low, not only MSM. If so, the levers are
   the heterosexual-male parameters (care-seeking, screening, mixing), not the MSM-het transmission split.

# 4. Evidence from the data

## 4.1 How the numbers are made

From the CDC surveillance reports (P&S diagnoses by sex, all MSAs, 1993-2019):

1. For two years, each city's change = log(end / start), for men and for women.
2. "Men minus women" = how far men moved compared with women.
3. Only cities with at least 20 cases for each sex in both years are used.
4. Count noise is removed from spreads. A count of N cases varies by chance with variance about N
   (Poisson), so log(N) varies with variance about 1/N, and a change between two years with about
   1/start + 1/end. The spread across cities = real spread + noise, so real = observed - average noise.

Cautions for all tables:

1. These are diagnoses, not transmission. An epidemic amplifies small changes in transmission, so the
   data values are upper bounds for the prior.
2. "Male" is all men, including heterosexual men; the true MSM-het differences are larger.
3. Mostly large cities (because of the 20-case minimum), and each row uses a different set of cities.

To regenerate (needs `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER`; data only, takes about a minute):

```{r regenerate}
source("applications/SHIELD/analysis/diagnostics/prior/check_spline_prior_against_data.R")
```

## 4.2 Table 1: average change by period (tests assumption A, expected change = 0)

| Period | Cities | Men | Women | Men - women | Men relative to women |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1993-1995 | 30 | -0.48 | -0.46 | -0.02 | x0.98 |
| 1995-2000 | 14 | -0.41 | -0.46 | 0.05 | x1.05 |
| **2000-2005** | 9 | **+0.89** | -0.23 | **+1.12** | **x3.05** |
| 2005-2010 | 10 | 0.26 | 0.10 | 0.15 | x1.17 |
| 2000-2010 | 7 | 1.50 | 0.07 | 1.43 | x4.18 |
| 2010-2019 | 14 | 0.60 | 0.50 | 0.10 | x1.10 |

1. The 1990s decline was shared: men and women fell together.
2. The divergence was one event, in 2000-2005 (the MSM resurgence), in every city with data.
3. After 2005, and in the recent rise (2010-2019), men and women moved nearly together.
4. So "expected change = 0" fits every step except 2000-2010.

## 4.3 Table 2: spread of change across cities, by gap length (tests assumption B, SD grows in proportion to years)

Each city's change minus that period's national average; SD across cities, count noise removed.

| Gap | 1y | 2y | 3y | 5y | 7y | 10y | 15y |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Men | 0.267 | 0.406 | 0.496 | 0.635 | 0.638 | 0.666 | 0.762 |
| Women | 0.264 | 0.443 | 0.559 | 0.671 | 0.657 | 0.698 | 0.705 |
| Men - women | 0.109 | 0.221 | 0.296 | 0.401 | 0.482 | 0.630 | 0.552 |
| Prior per group, now (proportional to years) | 0.020 | 0.041 | 0.061 | 0.101 | 0.142 | 0.203 | 0.304 |
| Prior per group, square root of years | 0.064 | 0.091 | 0.111 | 0.143 | 0.170 | 0.203 | 0.248 |
| Prior MSM - het, now | 0.016 | 0.031 | 0.047 | 0.079 | 0.110 | 0.157 | 0.236 |

How fast the spread grows (SD ~ years^power): men 0.37, women 0.35, **men - women 0.63**, prior now 1.

1. Per sex, the spread grows quickly for a few years and then levels off: unusual rises or falls in a city fade,
   and part of the 1-year spread is reporting swings.
2. The men - women spread keeps growing, roughly like the square root of years (a random walk), not in proportion to years.
3. The prior is 3-5x narrower than the data at 10 years, and up to 13x narrower at short gaps. With the
   square root of years it is about equally narrower at every gap.

## 4.4 Table 3: correlation of men's and women's change (tests assumption C, 0.7)

| Gap | 1y | 2y | 3y | 5y | 7y | 10y | 15y |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Correlation | 0.92 | 0.87 | 0.85 | 0.81 | 0.72 | 0.57 | 0.72 |

0.7 fits the 5- to 15-year spline steps. No change needed.

# 5. Verdict on each assumption

| | Assumption | Supported by the data? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spline points | Missing a point at 2005 for the sharp 2000-2005 shift (we decided this is not essential, section 6) |
| 2 | Baseline medians | No conflict (not pinned; the baseline is wide) |
| 3 | Baseline spread | No conflict |
| 4 | A. Expected change 0 | **No, for 2000-2010** (shared shift, men x4 relative to women); yes for other steps |
| 5 | TRATE_DELTA = 1.5 | Probably too tight; how much is unknown (diagnoses overstate transmission change) |
| 6 | B. SD proportional to years | **No**: grows close to the square root of years |
| 7 | C. Correlation 0.7 | Yes for 5- to 15-year steps |
| 8 | Steps independent | Cannot be tested with this data |

# 6. Candidate revisions

## 6.1 Spread grows with the square root of years (assumption B)

1. **Idea:** transmission changes a little each year in a random direction; over 10 years some changes cancel,
   so the total spread grows like sqrt(10), not 10.
2. **Evidence:** table 2 (men - women grows as years^0.63).
3. **Effect:** short 5-year steps get looser, the long 1970-1990 step tighter, the 10-year step stays the same.
   The 2010-2022 step gets its true length (12 years; now treated as 10).
4. **Code:** only the SDs passed to the prior change, not the function.

## 6.2 Raise TRATE_DELTA (the overall size of change)

1. **Idea:** one number sets how far transmission can move in 10 years (95% range x/÷ TRATE_DELTA).
2. **Evidence:** table 2; the prior is 3-5x narrower than the data at 10 years. It should be narrower
   (diagnoses amplify), but not necessarily that much. 2-2.5 is consistent with the data.
3. **Combine with 6.1** so one rule applies to every step.

Per-group SD and 95% range, square root of years, by TRATE_DELTA:

| Step | Years | Now (proportional, 1.5) | Sqrt, 1.5 | Sqrt, 2 | Sqrt, 2.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1970-1990 | 20 | 0.405 (x/÷ 2.25) | 0.287 (x/÷ 1.78) | 0.490 (x/÷ 2.66) | 0.648 (x/÷ 3.65) |
| 1990-1995, 1995-2000 | 5 | 0.101 (x/÷ 1.22) | 0.143 (x/÷ 1.33) | 0.245 (x/÷ 1.63) | 0.324 (x/÷ 1.91) |
| 2000-2010 | 10 | 0.203 (x/÷ 1.5) | 0.203 (x/÷ 1.5) | 0.347 (x/÷ 2.0) | 0.458 (x/÷ 2.5) |
| 2010-2022 | 12 | 0.203 (treated as 10) | 0.222 | 0.380 | 0.502 |

At TRATE_DELTA = 2, the MSM - het SD for 2000-2010 is 0.27 (data: 0.63 in diagnoses, so about half),
and the 2000-2010 shift in table 1 (+1.43) is about 5 SDs away instead of 9.

Code for 6.1 + 6.2:

```{r revision-sqrt}
# Spread of the transmission multiplier changes between spline years: SD grows with the square root of
# the number of years (a random walk). TRATE_DELTA = 95% fold range of a 10-year change (x/÷ TRATE_DELTA).
TRATE_DELTA <- 2
trate.step.sd <- function(years) 0.5 * log(TRATE_DELTA) * sqrt(years / 10)

    logsd.deltas.past   = c("1970" = trate.step.sd(20),   # 1970-1990
                            "1990" = trate.step.sd(5),    # 1990-1995
                            "1995" = trate.step.sd(5)),   # 1995-2000
    logsd.deltas.future = c("2010" = trate.step.sd(10),   # 2000-2010
                            "2022" = trate.step.sd(12)),  # 2010-2022
```

Check after a run: the historical penalty stays small (the 1970-1990 step widens slightly, x/÷ 2.66 vs 2.25).

## 6.3 Expect MSM to rise relative to heterosexuals in 2000-2010 (assumption A)

1. **Idea:** the prior says "expect no change" in every step. In 2000-2010 every city moved the same way, so let
   the prior expect MSM up and heterosexuals down in that step. 6.1 and 6.2 give more room; this moves the centre.
2. **Evidence:** table 1 (+1.43 over 2000-2010, +1.12 in 2000-2005, in diagnoses).
3. **Size:** about half of the observed shift, since diagnoses overstate transmission change; e.g. MSM +0.35,
   het -0.35 (MSM:het ratio x2). Run a second version at +0.5 / -0.5 to see how sensitive the fit is.
4. **Code:** `make.joint.mv.spline.prior` fixes every delta mean at 0 (`untransformed_mu`). Add an optional
   argument with default 0, so other uses do not change. A sketch (not tested):

```{r revision-mean-shift}
# new optional argument: named list of delta means per parameter and step year (default: all 0)
make.joint.mv.spline.prior <- function(parameters, logmean.baseline, logsd.baseline,
                                       logsd.deltas.past, logsd.deltas.future, spline.times,
                                       correlation = 0.5,
                                       logmean.deltas = list()) {
    # ... unchanged validation and sorting of logsd.deltas.past / logsd.deltas.future ...
    delta.years <- c(names(logsd.deltas.past), names(logsd.deltas.future))   # oldest to newest, as sorted
    delta.means <- unlist(lapply(delta.years, function(y) sapply(parameters, function(p) {
        v <- logmean.deltas[[p]][y]
        if (is.null(v) || is.na(v)) 0 else unname(v)
    })))
    untransformed_mu <- c(logmean.baseline, delta.means)                   # was: rep(0, ...) for the deltas
    # ... rest unchanged ...
}

# use:
make.joint.mv.spline.prior(...,
    logmean.deltas = list("transmission.rate.multiplier.msm"          = c("2010" =  0.35),
                          "transmission.rate.multiplier.heterosexual" = c("2010" = -0.35)))
```

## 6.4 Correlation

Keep 0.7 (table 3). A correlation per step would need a function change and is not supported strongly enough.

## 6.5 A spline point at 2005

Would match the sharp 2000-2005 shift, but adds two parameters. Set aside: for calibration and projection,
the levels by 2010 and the 2010-2022 trend matter more than the timing within the 2000s.

# 7. Plan after calib.10.20.stage1

1. Run, with `CALIBRATION.CODE <- "calib.10.20.stage1"`:
   - `fit/check_fit_by_sex_over_time.R`: does male P&S fit 2000-2014 now?
   - `prior/check_prior_position.R`: are the MSM - het 1995-2000 and 2000-2010 changes still pinned?
   - `fit/check_fit_by_age.R`: has 15-19 moved toward 1?
2. If male P&S still trails the data in 2000-2014 **and** MSM - het is still pinned: apply 6.1 + 6.2 (no function change).
3. If that is not enough: add 6.3.
4. If instead the gap is heterosexual men (MSM share too high while male P&S is too low): look at the
   heterosexual-male care-seeking, screening and mixing priors, not the transmission split.
5. Any of these is a stage-1 prior: rerun from stage 1, reusing calib.10.15.stage0.
